summary: A message that the University of Illinois Center for Advanced Computation would study whether network members could pool purchases of equipment and supplies to get better group prices. It notes two risks: too little shared demand and procurement rules requiring competitive bidding.

plainLanguage.summary: The University of Illinois planned to study whether network members could coordinate equipment purchases. Sites were asked to list their needs and acceptable alternatives.

questions: what was the network group purchasing study
what obstacles could prevent pooled purchases
subtitle: A feasibility study of coordinated equipment and supply purchases.

tldr.problem: Network members may need similar equipment and supplies, but individual purchasing might miss opportunities for shared negotiations.
tldr.mechanism: The University of Illinois Center for Advanced Computation planned to collect member requirements and assess whether manufacturers could offer group prices.
tldr.outcome: The study would examine whether shared demand and procurement rules made the idea workable; it did not establish a purchasing service.

today: RFC 249 describes a proposed purchasing study published in October 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: The Proposed Study
sections.content:
The Center for Advanced Computation at the University of Illinois agreed to study whether it could serve as a coordinating point for equipment and supply purchases for network members. It would compile common requirements and assess whether contacting manufacturers or distributors could produce group prices.

The results, including item listings and costs, would be passed to network members.
sections.plainLanguage: The Illinois center planned to find out whether network members could buy common equipment together. It would report possible prices and suppliers to the members.

sections.title: Potential Obstacles
sections.content:
The RFC identifies two main problems: there might not be enough demand for commonly needed items, and organizations might have competitive-bidding requirements for items that were not sole-source purchases.

The authors considered it premature to abandon the idea before collecting and analyzing the lists of items and suppliers. They also acknowledge the project might have to be abandoned.
sections.plainLanguage: Group buying could fail if too few members wanted the same items. Procurement rules requiring competitive bids could also make some shared purchases difficult.

sections.title: Information Requested
sections.content:
Network members were asked to send a list of equipment and supplies needed during the fiscal year, including acceptable alternatives. The RFC excludes 2400-foot magnetic tapes, tabulating cards and conventional printer paper from the initial request.

It gives examples of terminals, printers, graphics equipment, plotters, digitizers, computers and peripherals that might be included.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites were asked to list quantities, equipment and acceptable substitutes. Some common supplies were excluded from the request.
